intended_object: The R-algebra homomorphism R[t] → R[x₀,…,xₙ]/I_Hankel sending t to the class of x₀. It is the section of the coordinate-axis projection that sends x₀ ↦ t and xᵢ ↦ 0 for i ≠ 0. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body composes `Polynomial.aeval (MvPolynomial.X 0)` with `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (hankelIdeal R n)`. That is exactly the R-algebra map determined by t ↦ [x₀], and it is unique because R[t] is free on t. The library's lemmas `axisSection_X`, `axisSection_C` and `axisProjection_axisSection` confirm the intended behaviour: it is a right inverse of `axisProjection`. It is stated over an arbitrary commutative ring and every degree n, which is the natural generality of the Hankel presentation. It is a specific map, so its specificity does not make it too narrow. Mathlib has no dedicated counterpart; the map is assembled from Mathlib's general evaluation and quotient maps. One could see it as a helper for the split-surjection results, but it is a well-defined algebra homomorphism and the definition matches its description exactly.
